newsitem.title: USA: Seagram says it plans to continue television ads.
newsitem.headline: Seagram says it plans to continue television ads.

text.p: Seagram Co. Ltd. said Tuesday it would not pull its television whiskey advertisements in spite of renewed Congressional criticism that they are targeted to children.
U.S. Representative Joseph Kennedy, D-Mass, told reporters that Seagram's television ad campaign featuring a peacock and dogs "is directly targeted at children."

"Beer and wine companies have had unrestricted access to the TV airwaves that supply so much information about the benefits of drinking to the point that now ... Budweiser frogs are more readily identifiable to 5th graders in this country than Tony the Tiger or Bugs Bunny and a whole array of cartoon characters," he said.

All but one of greater Boston's local television stations and their local affiliates have pledged not to air the spot, he said and all but two television stations in New Hampshire have agreed to uphold the ban.
A spokesman for New England Cable News, which is airing the spot between 8 p.m. and midnight, said it will continue to air the advertising.

"This has been a black and white issue for broadcasters for many years and we think it's okay to deal in the grey a little bit," said NECN's David Buonfiglio. "The audience of New England Cable News is mature, upscale adults. Probably very, very few children will be able to see this ad on New England Cable News... I would consider (Seagram) to be a significant fourth quarter advertiser for us."
Federal Communication Commission Chairman Reed Hundt expressed concern Monday about the ads' impact on children, but did not say whether the agency would move to restrict their use.
Seagram spokeswoman Bevin Gove said the company would continue to run television and radio spots for Royal Crown and Chivas Regal.

She said the company decided to break the hard liquor industry's 48-year voluntary ban on broadcast advertising because it put Seagram at a competitive disadvantage against beer and wine companies that do advertise on television.
"We feel the time has come to access electronic advertising but to do it appropriately, responsibly and tastefully and that means advertising to responsible adults," said Gove.
She added that the Toronto-based company had not assessed the impact on sales of the negative reaction to the ads, which began airing onka local Texas television station in June.
